conviction_note: Three peers (Hilton US +7.0%, IHG US +6.9%, Hyatt US +8.2%) point to a clear Q3 RevPAR beat against Marriott's 3.5-4.0% guide. That beat is mostly priced: the stock is +11.8% in 20 days, within 0.7% of its 52-week high and above the mean analyst target, consensus EPS ($2.86) already sits above the top of the guide ($2.82), and the whisper is $2.92. The reaction will turn on the Q4/FY guide and early 2027 talk. Hilton's equivalent setup (Q3 beat, FY RevPAR raised, Q4 guide cautious on midterms and the Middle East, FY EBITDA midpoint up only $10M) traded down ~2.7% premarket, and Marriott's own last print fell 6.97% on a beat-and-raise with a soft next-quarter guide. So print_vs_bar is positive and the reaction leans slightly negative: p_up 45 on abs 4.5 gives -0.45. The findings sum to -1.2. That is larger because it adds up individually sized guide and positioning negatives that p_up holds near 50, given 5 of 7 prior prints rose and the skew is only moderate.
bar: Q3 adj EPS consensus $2.86 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/407878/marriotts-q3-test-can-us-momentum-and-new-card-deals-clear-a-bar-above-guidance), Benzinga $2.83 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MAR/earnings-forecasts). Whisper $2.92. Company guide: Q3 adj EPS $2.74-2.82, worldwide RevPAR +3.5-4.0%, gross fees $1,474-1,483M, adj EBITDA $1,439-1,468M; FY26 RevPAR +3.0-3.5%, adj EPS $11.64-11.81 (https://www.franchising.com/news/20260803_marriott_international_reports_second_quarter_2026_results.html). Revenue consensus ~$7.04B. Two estimate sources roughly agree ($2.83-2.86), so the bar is sourced. My read: RevPAR ~5-5.5% and EPS ~$2.88-2.92, about +1.5% over the $2.86 bar.
positioning_check: Short interest ~6.73M shares as of the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~4.2 days to cover, roughly 2.5% of float. Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism against a negative (https://massive.com/quote/mar, plus the equibles/curvedtrading history showing 4.6-5.5M in August: https://equibles.com/stocks/mar/short-interest). Baseline skew 25d is +2.54 vol points (downside paid, moderate). Put/call OI 0.65. Run-up +11.76% over 20d and +2.68% over 5d, 0.7% below the 52-week high. Price ~$401 is above the mean analyst target (~$371-387 per Benzinga/MarketBeat aggregations).

findings.finding: All three peers that reported Q3 2026 since Marriott last spoke beat on US RevPAR. Hilton US +7.0% (system +5.8% against its own ~4.0% Q3 guide), IHG US +6.9% (Americas +6.8%), Hyatt US +8.2% (system +7.2%, luxury +8.8%). Marriott's US&C was +5.0% in Q2 against Hilton US +5.4%. The same spread implies Marriott US&C of ~+6.5% and worldwide RevPAR of ~5-5.5%, against Marriott's Q3 guide of +3.5-4.0%. Each RevPAR point is worth roughly $15M of fees, so the fee beat is ~$20-25M, or about $0.05-0.06 of EPS over the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: RevPAR beat (3.4%, US&C +5.0%, best in 13 quarters) with the FY raised, stock -6.97% on a soft Q3 EPS guide. Q4 2025 print (2026-02-10): +8.5% on the 2026 outlook. Hilton on 2026-10-27, with an almost identical RevPAR beat, was -2.7% premarket. RevPAR beats alone have not been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. If the market had not absorbed the peer prints, MAR would be flat into the print and consensus would sit inside the guide. Instead the stock is +11.8% in 20 days, consensus EPS of $2.86 is above the $2.82 top of the guide, and the whisper is $2.92. The residual is that the size of the US beat (7-8% at peers) may exceed what the ~$2.86 consensus embeds.
findings.independence: IHG Q3 trading update 2026-10-22, US +6.9% (https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2026/third-quarter-trading-update-to-30-september-2026). Hyatt Q3 8-K 2026-10-29, US +8.2% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468174/000146817426000029/q32026earningsrelease.htm). STR weekly mid-September: record ADR and luxury/upper-upscale +11.1% (https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4134577/us-hotel-results-for-week-ending-19-september). These are three separate companies' documents.

findings.finding: Hilton's Q3 release set the template for the guide risk. It raised FY RevPAR to 4.0-4.5% but guided Q4 RevPAR to only +3.0-3.5%, citing midterm elections and a larger Middle East impact. Its FY adj EBITDA went to $4,060-4,080M from $4,040-4,080M (midpoint +$10M) despite a Q3 that beat its own EBITDA guide ($1,058M vs $1,035-1,055M), on lower Middle East and timeshare license-fee expectations. Marriott carries more Middle East exposure: management said ~35% of Middle East full-year revenue falls in Q4, against tough comps, and it has already flagged a midterm drag and Middle East construction delays.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAR 2026-08-03: RevPAR beat and FY raise but a next-quarter EPS guide ($2.74-2.82) below the ~$2.88 consensus, stock -6.97%. Guide direction has decided MAR's moves: +8.5% (Feb 2026, outlook) and -5.4% (Feb 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: MAR has risen since Hilton's 2026-10-27 print (+2.7% over 5 days, at the 52-week high), so the market has not applied Hilton's Q4 caution to Marriott, whose Middle East weight is larger. If it had, MAR would have traded down with HLT that week. Put skew of +2.54 is consistent with some hedge, but only moderately so.
findings.independence: Marriott's own Q2 call flagged Q4 below Q3, a midterm drag and 35% of Middle East revenue in Q4 (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/transcripts/MAR-2Q26-transcript). Hilton's EBITDA guide history, $4,040-4,080M after Q2 (https://www.webull.com/news/15306336762209280). Hilton premarket -2.7% (https://finviz.com/news/408894/hilton-shares-fall-27-as-q3-revenue-misses-forecasts-despite-higher-earnings). Shares the Hilton release document with finding 1.

findings.finding: The Middle East improved sharply in Q3 from Q2. Accor's UAE RevPAR was down ~20% in Q3, improving on Q2. Hilton's MEA was -5.6% and Hyatt's MEA -0.7%. Dubai occupancy reached 66% in August (89% of August 2025). Marriott's Middle East RevPAR was -43% in Q2 and management guided EMEA to improve in Q3. The Q3 incentive-fee hit is likely smaller than feared, but Accor's guide assumes only 'no deterioration' in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the Middle East drag (-43%) was cited as why revenue missed and international fell 0.5%, stock -6.97%. No prior print shows the line surprising positively.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the run-up. Marriott does not disclose Middle East monthly data, so the size of the Q3 improvement in its mostly managed (incentive-fee-heavy) portfolio is not known until the print. If it were fully priced, previews would not still list the Middle East as the main offset to US strength.
findings.independence: Hilton MEA -5.6% (SEC 8-K above); Hyatt MEA -0.7% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468174/000146817426000029/q32026earningsrelease.htm); Dubai DET August occupancy 66% (https://gulfbusiness.com/en/2026/tourism/dubai-hotel-occupancy-climbs-to-66-in-august-as-tourism-picks-up/). It is a proxy for Marriott's own number. It uses the same Middle East exposure as finding 2, but for Q3, where finding 2 is about Q4.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is stretched. MAR is +11.8% in 20 days, 0.7% off its 52-week high and above the mean analyst target. Consensus EPS of $2.86 already sits above the $2.82 top of the guide and the whisper is $2.92. Earnings Whispers notes a stock 'priced for momentum may gain little if guidance only holds steady'. A modest beat is in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a +9.4% run following Q1, MAR rose only +1.28% on the Q2-period print of 2026-05-06; after a run-up into 2026-08-03 it fell 6.97% on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding says the bar has moved above the guide, so the fundamental beat in finding 1 is needed just to stand still. If this were not the case, the stock would sit near its post-Q2 level (~$344-370) rather than at $401.
findings.independence: The baseline tape (run_up_20d 11.76%, pct_from_52w_high -0.7%, skew +2.54) is independent of the article. The analyst target average of ~$371-387 is from MarketBeat/Benzinga aggregations (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MAR/price-targets).

findings.finding: October US industry data started Q4 well against an easy comp. STR's week of 11-17 October 2026 showed US RevPAR +5.5% (occupancy +3.1%). The comparable weeks of October 2025 were weak: the week ending 25 October 2025 was -5.3%, during the US government shutdown. So Marriott's Q4 US&C guide has easy comps, which may let it guide above Hilton's cautious 3.0-3.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 guide tone decided the -6.97% (Q2) and +8.5% (Q4 2025) moves. No direct history of October data moving MAR.
findings.why_not_priced: Weekly STR data is public, but Hilton guided Q4 cautiously anyway. If the market believed the easy-comp argument, Hilton would not have traded down on its Q4 guide. It is a proxy and is sized small.
findings.independence: October 2025 comparison week -5.3% (https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4129571.html). This is an industry proxy, not Marriott's number.

findings.finding: Net rooms growth is tracking the low end of 4.5-5% because of Middle East construction delays, against Hilton's ~6% and the ~6-7% FY guide. Investment spending (key money) was raised to up to $1.35B, and owned/leased guidance was cut twice. The unit-growth gap to Hilton is a standing multiple question that the Q3 print updates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NUG commentary was part of the Q2 call that preceded the -6.97% move; not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August, so largely priced. The residual is whether Q3 NUG slips below 4.5%, which no source can see in advance.
findings.independence: Hilton NUG 6.0% (Hilton 8-K above); Earnings Whispers preview notes the owned/leased cuts and key money (finviz URL above).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call, management said 2027 group pace was roughly flat (rate up, room nights down slightly) and that 2026 pace could moderate. 2027 also laps the World Cup (~45bp of 2026 global RevPAR). A Q3 call update on 2027 is a risk to the out-year narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAR's Q3 calls have historically carried preliminary next-year commentary. The 2025-11-04 print rose +3.16% on early 2026 colour.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced as an August fact. The new information is the Q3 update to it. With the stock at highs, a flat 2027 group book has less cushion than it did at $344.
findings.independence: None directly. It shares the Q2 transcript with finding 6.

findings.finding: Newly signed US co-brand card agreements with Chase and Amex add ~$30M of 2026 fees in H2 (about half landing in Q3), with $100-125M targeted by 2028 at a 26% royalty. This is already inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The card-fee outlook helped the +8.5% on 2026-02-10 per contemporaneous coverage. Inside guidance since August.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside guidance and is in every preview, so it is priced. The only residual is any raise to the 2028 target.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (finviz URL above). It shares the Q2 transcript with findings 6 and 7.

findings.finding: The 8-K of 2026-09-24 amended and restated the revolver: $5.0B (from $4.5B), with an accordion to $5.5B and maturity extended to 2031 from 2027. No borrowings were disclosed. $1.25B of notes was issued in August. This is routine refinancing to fund buybacks (> $4.5B FY capital return), not distress.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and immaterial. The money funds the capital-return program, and the investment-grade revolver is unchanged in terms.
findings.independence: EDGAR 8-K list shows a 2026-09-24 filing with items 1.01/2.03 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001048286&type=8-K).

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the moderate put skew (+2.54) and treats the +11.8% run-up as having priced the peer-implied RevPAR beat. The fundamental read (a beat) cuts against the skew, and the reaction read (guide risk, stretched positioning) agrees with it, so p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3 / one entity in both directions: the Middle East Q3 recovery (finding 3) and the Q4 Middle East drag (finding 2) use the same exposure. I kept them apart because they are different quarters, and cut the positive from +0.4 to +0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the October STR easy-comp finding is an industry proxy, cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
2027 group pace was cut from -0.4 to -0.3 because it shares the August transcript with the NUG and card findings, and its update is uncertain.

The peer-print read-through was kept at +0.8: the 'what worked' section names exactly this pattern (a peer's print after the company last spoke), but the consensus is not stale here, because it already sits above the guide.

Lessons 4 and 7 changed nothing: the financing is routine (sized 0), and short interest of ~2.5% of float is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for a squeeze. Lesson 1 was already reflected in p_up 45 on a confirmed beat.
